name: Portugal
tagline: Cheap for EU students, but the EU route is the Portuguese one
summary: Portugal has two completely separate front doors, and an EU/EEA student must use the national one. Non-EU students use the Estatuto do Estudante Internacional, apply straight to a university, and pay somewhere between €3,500 and €16,500 a year. EU/EEA citizens are legally excluded from that route and must go through the Concurso Nacional de Acesso, the same national contest Portuguese school-leavers use. The payoff is the price: the capped public tuition (propina) was €697 for 2025/26. The catch is that the national contest is built around Portuguese school exams and mostly leads to Portuguese-taught degrees.
whyConsider: Public tuition is capped: €697 a year for a licenciatura in 2025/26, and EU students pay exactly that
Nova SBE charged EU students €697 while charging international-statute students €7,500 for the same degree (2025/26 figures) — the EU passport is worth real money here
Living costs outside Lisbon are low by Western European standards
A small but genuine set of English-taught bachelors in business and economics at Nova SBE and Católica Lisbon
The academic year timetable is late, so you apply after you have your IB results rather than on predictions
watchOuts: As an EU citizen you cannot use the Estatuto do Estudante Internacional — it explicitly excludes EU/EEA nationals, so the easy English-language route is closed to you

The Concurso Nacional de Acesso requires an equivalence certificate for your foreign secondary education plus provas de ingresso, which you satisfy either by sitting Portuguese national exams or by substituting homologous foreign exams
The list of foreign exams recognised as homologous is republished each year by 31 May, so you cannot plan more than a year ahead with certainty
Portuguese is required for most degrees; even the University of Porto's international route demands Portuguese at independent-user level
The whole national contest runs in late July and August, which is very late if you also need housing and a fallback

ibRecognition.subjectLevelRule: Not defined nationally. For the national contest what matters is whether your IB subject exams can be accepted as homologous substitutes for specific provas de ingresso. Private institutions such as Católica set their own IB rules. Nova SBE's 36 points (Mathematics HL at 6 or better) for Economics and Management, and 34 for Ocean Studies, are the rules of its international route, which is closed to EU citizens.
ibRecognition.gradeConversion: For the Concurso Nacional de Acesso, foreign final exam grades are converted onto the Portuguese 0–200 scale using formulas published by DGES, with separate formulas for numerical and alphabetic grading systems.
notes: You need a certificate of equivalence confirming your foreign secondary course is equivalent to Portuguese secondary education. This is requested from a Portuguese public or private secondary school, or from the Direção-Geral da Educação.
Documents must be apostilled or consularly legalised and translated into Portuguese.

The Comissão Nacional de Acesso ao Ensino Superior publishes the list of foreign exams accepted as homologous to Portuguese provas de ingresso annually, by 31 May of the application year. Exams sat from 2022 onwards remain valid for five years.
If you request substitution of provas de ingresso by foreign exams you must apply in the earlier priority window of the first phase, not the ordinary deadline.
Private institutions such as Católica accept the IB directly with their own minimum scores and do not depend on this machinery.

deadlines.label: University of Porto — special contest for international students, phase 1 (not for EU citizens)
deadlines.notes: Listed for completeness. EU citizens cannot use this route: U.Porto runs it for applicants "who do not have Portuguese nationality or the nationality of another member state of the European Union". U.Porto offered 712 places across this contest for 2026/27.

deadlines.label: University of Porto — special contest for international students, phase 2 (not for EU citizens)
deadlines.notes: Not open to EU citizens; see phase 1.

deadlines.label: Nova SBE — international bachelor admission, autumn intake (not for EU/EEA citizens)
deadlines.notes: Published as "From April 14 to June 16, 2026, until 5.00 pm Lisbon time"; the time is the closing time. EU/EEA citizens cannot use this route. The page states that international student status does not apply to nationals of an EU Member State or of a state signatory to the EEA Agreement, so an EU applicant to Nova SBE goes through the Concurso Nacional de Acesso instead. Listed for completeness. The spring intake is a separate entry.

deadlines.label: University of Porto — special contest for international students, phase 3 (not for EU citizens)
deadlines.notes: Not open to EU citizens; see phase 1.

deadlines.label: Concurso Nacional de Acesso — 1st phase applications: candidates substituting provas de ingresso with foreign exams, and the emigrant priority quota
deadlines.notes: This is the deadline that applies to an IB candidate, and it is a week earlier than the one everybody else sees. DGES's Portuguese calendar page names the group as "candidatos com pedido de substituição de provas de ingresso por exames estrangeiros" and gives them 20 a 29 de julho, against 20 de julho a 06 de agosto for the rest. If you are asking a Portuguese university to accept IB subjects in place of the Portuguese provas de ingresso — which is the normal route for an IB candidate — you are in this group. The 2026 calendar was approved by Despacho n.º 9359-A/2026 of 23 July 2026; the 2027 calendar will be approved by its own despacho and is not published yet.

deadlines.label: Concurso Nacional de Acesso — 1st phase applications, all other candidates
deadlines.notes: Published as "20 de julho a 06 de agosto". Do not plan against this date if you are substituting provas de ingresso with foreign exams — that group closes on 29 July and has its own entry. The 2026 calendar was approved by Despacho n.º 9359-A/2026 of 23 July 2026. The 2027 calendar will be published separately — re-check it.

deadlines.label: Concurso Nacional de Acesso — 1st phase results
deadlines.notes: Placement lists go to the institutions the day before publication.

deadlines.label: Concurso Nacional de Acesso — 1st phase enrolment
deadlines.notes: Published in Portuguese as "Matrícula: 24 a 27 de agosto". Four days from the placement list to being enrolled, which is why a fallback and a place to live matter before the result arrives.

deadlines.label: Concurso Nacional de Acesso — 2nd phase applications
deadlines.notes: DGES publishes the places left for this phase while the window is open (on 1 September in 2026); you do not have to do anything then. The date you act on is the closing date.

deadlines.label: Concurso Nacional de Acesso — 2nd phase results
deadlines.notes: Published as results on 30 September, with enrolment in the three days after.

deadlines.label: Concurso Nacional de Acesso — 2nd phase enrolment
deadlines.notes: Three days, starting the day after the placement list.

deadlines.label: Concurso Nacional de Acesso — 3rd phase applications
deadlines.notes: A three-day window. The places for the third phase are announced the day before it opens (9 October in 2026). DGES must decide any complaints about its results by 16 November 2026; that deadline binds DGES, not you.

deadlines.label: Concurso Nacional de Acesso — 3rd phase results
deadlines.notes: Results and the start of enrolment fall on the same day, 18 October.

deadlines.label: Concurso Nacional de Acesso — 3rd phase enrolment
deadlines.notes: It opens on the day the results appear and closes two days later.

deadlines.label: Nova SBE — international bachelor admission, spring intake (not for EU/EEA citizens)
deadlines.notes: Published as "From November 10 to December 4, 2026, until 5.00 pm Lisbon time"; the time is the closing time. Same eligibility rule: international student status does not apply to EU or EEA nationals, so EU/EEA citizens cannot use this route. It is listed because it falls in this window and is easy to mistake for an EU-open one.

deadlines.label: CNAES list of foreign exams accepted in place of provas de ingresso — republished
deadlines.notes: The deadline the whole substitution route depends on, and it is a publication date rather than something you do. DGES states it in Portuguese as "A CNAES divulga, anualmente, até 31 maio do ano da candidatura, uma deliberação com a lista dos exames finais estrangeiros homólogos" — the list is republished by 31 May of the year you apply in, so until then you cannot be certain which IB subjects will be accepted in place of which provas de ingresso. It lands under two months before the 29 July substitution deadline.

steps: Confirm early that you are treated as an EU candidate, not an international student — Decreto-Lei n.º 36/2014 excludes EU/EEA nationals from the international-student statute.
Apply to a Portuguese secondary school or the Direção-Geral da Educação for a certificate of equivalence for your IB Diploma, with apostilled and translated documents. Start this a year ahead.
Check which provas de ingresso your target degree requires, and whether the CNAES list published by 31 May recognises an IB exam as homologous. If not, you must sit the Portuguese national exams.
Register with DGES and submit the national contest application in the first phase, using the earlier priority deadline if you are substituting foreign exams.
Rank your choices — the national contest lets you list several degree-and-institution pairs in order of preference.
Wait for the placement list, then enrol within the short window that follows (typically three or four days).
If you miss out, use the second or third phase, or apply directly to a private institution such as Católica Lisbon.
application.selectionNotes: The national contest is a pure ranking exercise. Each degree has a fixed number of places and a cut-off (nota do último colocado) driven by demand. Your rank comes from your converted secondary grade plus your provas de ingresso results on the 0–200 scale, weighted as the institution specifies. Private institutions and the international contest run their own selection instead.

language.englishTaughtBachelors: Small. English-taught bachelor's degrees exist mainly in business and economics (Nova SBE, Católica Lisbon) with a scattering elsewhere. No official national count is given here.
language.englishProof: Set by each institution. Nova SBE and Católica accept standard English evidence; check the exact IB English grade each accepts.
notes: Most public university degrees are taught in Portuguese, and the national contest is designed around Portuguese-taught programmes.
Even the University of Porto's contest for international students states that applicants need Portuguese at independent-user level.
Portuguese is not hard to start once you are there, but it is not optional if you go the public-university route.

tuitionEuEea.value: €697 a year (maximum propina for CTeSP, licenciatura and integrated master's), payable in at least seven monthly instalments. Institutions may not exceed the previous year's cap. Small extras apply — Nova SBE adds €36.50 for administration and insurance.

tuitionNonEu.value: Set by each institution under the Estatuto do Estudante Internacional. The University of Porto publishes a range of €3,500 to €16,500 a year (2026/27 call); Nova SBE charges €7,500 a year, a figure it labels as valid for 2025/26. Católica Lisbon, which is private, charges non-EU students €858 a month over ten months (2026-27).

costs.applicationFee: Nova SBE charges €70 for the international bachelor application plus a €750 enrolment fee that is deducted from tuition. Católica Lisbon charges €180 (€100 early-bird in its first three rounds), then €450 on a conditional offer and €470 on enrolment (2026-27, non-refundable). No application fee was found for the national contest.
notes: The €697 figure is the legal maximum, not an average — some institutions charge less.

Parliament kept the cap frozen at €697 for 2026/27 in the 2026 State Budget, according to press reports; DGES's own page still gives only the 2025/26 figure, so treat 2026/27 and 2027/28 as unconfirmed.
For master's and doctoral programmes institutions set their own fees; the cap only covers the first cycle.
Nationals of Portuguese-speaking (CPLP) countries can get reductions of up to 45% on international-statute fees — not relevant to an EU/EEA student, but it explains fee tables you will see.
No official living-cost figure is quoted here.
Private Católica Lisbon charges EU students €780 a month over ten months — about €7,800 a year (2026-27), more than eleven times the public cap.

funding.note: The programme must be SU-approved, and outside the Nordics SU is capped at four years (48 klip).

funding: Portuguese state need-based grants (bolsas de ação social) administered by DGES and the institutions' social services; EU students are generally eligible; check the residence conditions with DGES.
Nova SBE and Católica run their own merit and need-based scholarships for bachelor students.
Erasmus+ for an exchange period inside the degree.
workRights: EU/EEA citizens have full labour-market access in Portugal with no permit. Non-EU students on a study residence permit may work part-time; check the current hour limit on the permit.
residency: Travel on your EU/EEA passport or national ID card. For stays over three months, EU citizens register at the local câmara municipal and receive a Certificado de Registo de Cidadão da União Europeia. You will also need a NIF (tax number) from the Finanças office almost immediately — rental contracts, bank accounts and phone contracts all require it.
housing: Public universities have limited residências with means-tested places; most students rent rooms in shared flats. Lisbon rents have risen sharply and are the main practical obstacle to studying there. Porto is cheaper, and Braga, Coimbra, Aveiro and Faro are cheaper again. Because the national contest only places you in late August, look for housing before you know your result, and be ready to move quickly.
healthcare: Bring a European Health Insurance Card for short stays. Once you register as a resident and have a NIF you can register with a local health centre (centro de saúde) under the Serviço Nacional de Saúde and be assigned a family doctor.

institutions.name: Nova School of Business and Economics
institutions.englishBachelors: Bachelors in Economics, Management and Ocean Studies, taught in English
institutions.note: A beachfront campus twenty minutes from Lisbon, teaching in English. An EU passport changes the price from €7,500 to €697 (2025/26), through the national contest.

institutions.name: Católica Lisbon School of Business & Economics
institutions.englishBachelors: English-taught undergraduate programmes in business and economics
institutions.note: Private, internationally accredited, and an English-taught business school an EU applicant can apply to directly, in rounds from December. Tuition for EU students is €780 a month over ten months (2026-27).

institutions.name: Universidade de Lisboa
institutions.englishBachelors: Very limited at bachelor level; most first-cycle teaching is in Portuguese
institutions.note: Formed by merging the classical and technical universities of Lisbon, and home to Instituto Superior Técnico.

institutions.name: Instituto Superior Técnico
institutions.englishBachelors: Bachelor teaching is largely in Portuguese; English appears mainly at master's level
institutions.note: The engineering school of ULisboa, with very high national contest cut-offs.

institutions.name: Universidade NOVA de Lisboa
institutions.englishBachelors: Concentrated in Nova SBE; limited elsewhere at bachelor level
institutions.note: A modern, decentralised university whose business school is its best-known international face.

institutions.name: ISCTE — Instituto Universitário de Lisboa
institutions.englishBachelors: Some English-taught undergraduate offer in management and international studies
institutions.note: A public university in central Lisbon with a strong social-science and business focus and a practical, employment-oriented reputation.

institutions.name: Universidade do Porto
institutions.englishBachelors: Limited at bachelor level; most first-cycle programmes are in Portuguese
institutions.note: A large university with 15 faculties and around 54,000 students, in a city much cheaper than Lisbon.

institutions.name: Universidade do Minho
institutions.note: A research-strong university in the north with notably low living costs and a large student population relative to the city.

institutions.name: Universidade de Coimbra
institutions.note: Founded in 1290 and a UNESCO World Heritage site, with a strongly traditional student culture.

institutions.name: Universidade de Aveiro
institutions.note: A modern campus university with a strong engineering and materials reputation, in a small coastal city.

institutions.name: Universidade do Algarve
institutions.englishBachelors: A small English-taught offer, mainly in marine and tourism-related fields
institutions.note: The southern coastal option, cheap to live in, with genuine strength in marine science.

institutions.name: Universidade Católica Portuguesa
institutions.englishBachelors: English-taught undergraduate programmes mainly through Católica Lisbon and its Porto business school
institutions.note: A private university that runs its own admissions outside the national contest. Its main site is in Portuguese; English-taught programmes are advertised faculty by faculty, and Católica Lisbon has its own English site.
